boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Reed College
boards.description: Ten publicly accessible Portland food and convenience destinations with currently documented late hours; verify hours before leaving.

cards.title: Taco Bell on SE Powell
cards.subtitle: 4933 SE Powell Blvd, Portland
cards.notes: Use the drive-thru when you need a food stop after most nearby counters have closed; confirm the ordering format before heading out.
cards.short_summary: A SE Powell drive-thru with exceptionally late published hours.
cards.evidence_claim: The official location page lists drive-thru service from 7 a.m. to 3 a.m. every day.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists drive-thru hours of 7 a.m.–3 a.m. daily; dine-in hours are listed separately and end earlier.

cards.entity_name: Taco Bell, 8181 SE Johnson Creek Blvd
cards.title: Taco Bell on SE Johnson Creek
cards.subtitle: 8181 SE Johnson Creek Blvd, Portland
cards.notes: Keep this as a later-hours option on the southeast side; use the published location page to check service details before leaving campus.
cards.short_summary: A southeast Portland drive-thru open into the early morning.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell's Portland locations page lists this restaurant as open until 3 a.m. and identifies it as an open-late drive-thru location.
cards.source_title: Taco Bell Restaurants in Portland, Oregon
cards.access_notes: The official Portland locator lists 8181 SE Johnson Creek Blvd as open until 3 a.m., with drive-thru and Open Late services.

cards.title: Krispy Kreme on SE 82nd
cards.subtitle: 9950 SE 82nd Ave, Portland
cards.notes: Choose this for a late bakery stop on SE 82nd; check the store page again for holiday exceptions before making a dedicated trip.
cards.short_summary: A Portland doughnut shop with published 24-hour access.
cards.evidence_claim: Krispy Kreme's official location page identifies the 9950 SE 82nd Ave shop as open 24 hours.
cards.access_notes: Official location page states “Open 24 Hours.”

cards.title: Baby Doll Pizza SE
cards.subtitle: 2835 SE Stark St, Portland
cards.notes: Plan a pizza pickup around the posted weekend window, and use the contact page to confirm the day’s service before traveling across town.
cards.short_summary: SE Stark pizza with a documented midnight Friday–Saturday close.
cards.evidence_claim: Baby Doll Pizza lists its SE Stark location as open until midnight on Fridays and Saturdays.
cards.source_title: Baby Doll Pizza — Contact and Hours
cards.access_notes: Official hours list 11 a.m.–midnight Friday and Saturday; Sunday through Thursday close at 11 p.m.

cards.title: Sizzle Pie Downtown
cards.subtitle: 949 SW Oak St, Portland
cards.notes: Use the downtown shop for a clearly timed late pizza pickup, and check its location page before going in case operating hours change.
cards.short_summary: Downtown pizza with a published midnight closing time every day.
cards.evidence_claim: Sizzle Pie's official Downtown location page lists hours of 11 a.m. to midnight every day.
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists 11 a.m.–midnight every day.

cards.title: Lúc Lác Vietnamese Kitchen
cards.subtitle: 835 SW 2nd Ave, Portland
cards.notes: For an evening meal downtown, check the restaurant’s current dinner window and place a pickup order before the published kitchen close.
cards.short_summary: Downtown Vietnamese restaurant with dinner service through 11 p.m.
cards.evidence_claim: Lúc Lác's official site lists dinner every day from 4 p.m. to 11 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Official site lists dinner daily, 4–11 p.m.; its patio also closes at 11 p.m.

cards.title: Voodoo Doughnut Old Town
cards.subtitle: 22 SW 3rd Ave, Portland
cards.notes: Use this Old Town doughnut counter only for a straightforward food pickup, and recheck its official location listing for day-specific changes.
cards.short_summary: The original Portland Voodoo location offers nearly round-the-clock doughnuts.
cards.evidence_claim: Voodoo Doughnut's official site says its shops are open “almost” 24 hours, and its Old Town ordering page identifies the 22 SW 3rd Ave location.
cards.access_notes: The official site describes Voodoo as open “almost” 24 hours; confirm the Old Town shop’s current hours before travel.

cards.title: WinCo Foods on SE Powell
cards.subtitle: 7979 SE Powell Blvd, Portland
cards.notes: Make a grocery-list stop rather than relying on restaurant service; check the store finder for holiday exceptions and current department availability.
cards.short_summary: A SE Powell grocery destination with corporate 24-hour operating guidance.
cards.evidence_claim: WinCo identifies its Portland-Powell store at 7979 SE Powell Blvd, and its official FAQ says most WinCo locations operate 24 hours a day, seven days a week.
cards.access_notes: WinCo states most locations are open 24 hours daily, with holiday exceptions; confirm this specific store before travel.

cards.title: Plaid Pantry at 82nd and Duke
cards.subtitle: 6440 SE 82nd & Duke, Portland
cards.notes: Use this convenience stop for a quick essentials run; the location page lists amenities and lets you confirm availability before you leave.
cards.short_summary: A Southeast Portland convenience store listed as open around the clock.
cards.evidence_claim: Plaid Pantry's official page for 82nd and Duke lists the store's hours as open 24 hours every day.
cards.access_notes: Official store page lists Open 24 hours for Monday through Sunday.

cards.title: Banning's Restaurant & Pie House
cards.subtitle: 11477 SW Pacific Hwy, Tigard
cards.notes: Save this for a planned Friday or Saturday diner-style meal; the official directions page shows a later weekend close than the rest of the week.
cards.short_summary: A Tigard restaurant with documented 11 p.m. Friday–Saturday hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Banning's official directions page lists Friday and Saturday hours from 7 a.m. to 11 p.m.
cards.source_title: Banning's Restaurant & Pie House — Directions and Hours
cards.access_notes: Official hours list Friday–Saturday, 7 a.m.–11 p.m.; other listed days end at 10 p.m.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Reed spaces documented for studying, making, meeting, performing, and student-led activity.

cards.title: Student Center
cards.subtitle: Lounge, study, and meeting space
cards.notes: Bring your work or a small group, then use the reservable rooms when available; card-swipe access is required.
cards.short_summary: A campus hub with space for independent work and group meetings.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed says the Student Center is open to students for lounging, studying, and meeting, with spaces reservable for individual or group use.
cards.source_title: Student Spaces — Office for Student Engagement
cards.access_notes: Listed hours are 8:30 AM–midnight daily; card swipe is required.

cards.title: Student Union
cards.subtitle: Gray Campus Center gathering space
cards.notes: Use the shared building for a late study session or a planned event, and enter through the northwest doors with your swipe access.
cards.short_summary: A centrally located student space adjacent to the Quad.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed identifies the Student Union as a student space and says it is open 24 hours during the academic year when classes are in session.
cards.source_title: Student Spaces — Office for Student Engagement
cards.access_notes: During the academic year, it is open 24 hours except college breaks; northwest-door swipe access is required.

cards.title: Publications Office
cards.subtitle: GCC 047 student-publication workspace
cards.notes: If you contribute to a student publication, coordinate with its editors before using this GCC workspace for reporting, layout, or production.
cards.short_summary: A designated workroom for Reed’s student publications.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed lists the Publications Office in GCC 047 as working space for the college’s various student publications.
cards.source_title: Student Spaces — Office for Student Engagement
cards.access_notes: Check student-space access guidelines and publication-specific arrangements before entering.

cards.title: Pool Hall
cards.subtitle: Student-run games and music space
cards.notes: Drop in to play pool, listen to the jukebox, or spend time with the writing on the walls; ask the manager about access details.
cards.short_summary: A six-table student space built around pool, music, and conversation.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed describes the Pool Hall as an all-access space with six pool tables, a jukebox, and a furnished office.
cards.access_notes: The college calls it an all-access space; confirm current access with the Pool Hall manager.

cards.title: Print Shoppe
cards.subtitle: Gray Campus Center screen-printing space
cards.notes: Plan a shirt or poster project and check in with the student-run shop before using its screen-printing equipment; bring your own blank garment.
cards.short_summary: A student-run place to make screen-printed projects.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed says the Print Shoppe is a student-run silk-screening space in Gray Campus Center with equipment for printing T-shirts.
cards.access_notes: Coordinate use and equipment access with the student-run Print Shoppe.

cards.title: Reed Bike Co-op
cards.subtitle: Guided bicycle-repair workshop
cards.notes: Bring your bike for guided repair, learn a maintenance task, and use the available tools with help from the co-op’s mechanics.
cards.short_summary: A hands-on workshop for repairing bikes and learning mechanical skills.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed says its Bike Co-op guides people through their own repairs and helps students become mechanics who can assist others.
cards.access_notes: Ask the co-op about current workshop access and availability of replacement items.

cards.title: Student Darkroom
cards.subtitle: Black-and-white photo developing space
cards.notes: Sign up for a training or refresher, then develop and print black-and-white photographs using the student darkroom’s shared materials.
cards.short_summary: A student space for learning and practicing analog black-and-white photography.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed says the Student Darkroom provides free loaner cameras, film, chemicals, paper, and training for black-and-white photography.
cards.access_notes: Free trainings are offered; seek a refresher if you need help using the space.

cards.title: Performing Arts Building
cards.subtitle: Atrium, rooftop patio, and performance rooms
cards.notes: Look for a public performance or campus event, then pause in the atrium or rooftop patio; respect rooms reserved for classes and productions.
cards.short_summary: A shared arts building with flexible theatres, rehearsal rooms, and gathering areas.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed says the Performing Arts Building has common spaces for collaborative work, a rooftop garden, exhibition spaces, and an atrium.
cards.access_notes: Performance and classroom spaces may be scheduled; use public or permitted areas only.

cards.title: Eliot Hall Chapel
cards.subtitle: Friday at Four concert setting
cards.notes: Check the music calendar for a Friday at Four program, then attend the performance in the chapel when the event is open to the community.
cards.short_summary: A historic chapel used for recurring student, staff, and guest performances.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed’s music department says the Chapel in historic Eliot Hall is used for Friday at Four concerts featuring staff, students, and guest performers.
cards.access_notes: Attend during a listed program or other authorized event; verify the current calendar before going.

cards.title: Vollum College Center
cards.subtitle: Map-listed lecture hall and lounge
cards.notes: Use the lounge for a change of study setting, and check campus listings before attending any lecture scheduled in the building.
cards.short_summary: A campus building with both lounge and lecture-hall functions.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed’s current campus map identifies Vollum College Center as containing a lecture hall and lounge.
cards.access_notes: Access can vary with classes, lectures, and campus operations.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: No-cost Reed activities and campus resources with direct current institutional evidence.

cards.entity_name: Douglas F. Cooley Memorial Art Gallery
cards.title: See the Cooley Gallery
cards.subtitle: Hauser Memorial Library
cards.notes: Bring a friend to view the current exhibition in Hauser Memorial Library; check the gallery calendar before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A free public art-gallery visit on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed states that the Cooley Gallery is free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Open Thursday–Sunday, noon–5 p.m., during an exhibition run.

cards.title: Join Community Dance
cards.subtitle: Performing Arts Building, Room 240
cards.notes: Drop into a weekly creative-movement session with a friend; no prior dance experience or registration is required.
cards.short_summary: A no-registration community dance session.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed’s Spring 2026 Community Dance sessions are free and open to the public, with no registration required.
cards.access_notes: The listed Spring 2026 sessions are Thursdays, 6:10–7:30 p.m.; review the page for exceptions and waiver details.

cards.entity_name: Reed College Politics and Policy Lecture Series
cards.title: Attend a policy lecture
cards.subtitle: Reed College campus
cards.notes: Watch the series page for a scheduled speaker, then bring a question or stay afterward to compare notes with friends.
cards.short_summary: Public talks on politics and policy.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed says all Politics and Policy Lecture Series events are free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Check the series page for announced events and locations.

cards.title: Browse student research posters
cards.subtitle: Reed College campus
cards.notes: Visit the showcase when announced and make a mini route through projects that span different majors and summer research topics.
cards.short_summary: A public poster-session view of Reed student work.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed identifies the President’s Student Showcase as free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Check the showcase page for the next event date and location.

cards.title: Get bike repair support
cards.subtitle: Gray Campus Center student spaces
cards.notes: Bring a bike issue to the student-led co-op and ask for repair support; confirm access details through Student Engagement.
cards.short_summary: Student bike-repair help without a purchase.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed describes the Bike Co-op as a student-led space offering students free bike repair support.
cards.access_notes: For Reed students; review Student Engagement access guidance before visiting.

cards.title: Check out a library book
cards.subtitle: Hauser Memorial Library
cards.notes: Choose a book together, set aside quiet reading time, and use a Reed student library card to check it out.
cards.short_summary: Borrow from Reed’s library collection with a free student card.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed states that all Reed students and faculty can get a free library card.
cards.access_notes: Available to Reed students and faculty; library borrowing terms apply.

cards.title: Stop by the Community Pantry
cards.subtitle: Gray Campus Center, Lower Level Room 042
cards.notes: Coordinate a practical pantry stop with a friend and check the posted schedule before going; it serves the Reed community.
cards.short_summary: A no-cost basic-needs resource in the Gray Campus Center.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed says the Community Pantry provides food, toiletries, hygiene products, and more at no cost to Reed community members.
cards.access_notes: Open to Reed students, faculty, and staff; check the pantry page for current hours and closures.

cards.title: Take part in International Orientation
cards.subtitle: Reed College campus
cards.notes: Eligible incoming students can register for orientation sessions, mentor connections, and the scheduled Portland outing before the deadline.
cards.short_summary: No-cost orientation activities for eligible incoming international students.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed says International Student Orientation has no registration fee and that its meals, sessions, and activities are covered by Reed.
cards.access_notes: Fall 2026 is listed for August 21–24; required for F-1 and J-1 visa holders, with opt-in availability noted for eligible U.S. passportholders and permanent residents.

cards.entity_name: Multicultural Resource Center Peer Mentor Program
cards.title: Connect through the Peer Mentor Program
cards.subtitle: Multicultural Resource Center
cards.notes: Incoming first-year students can apply for the mentor program to meet peers and join its pre-orientation activities if accepted.
cards.short_summary: A no-fee peer-connection program for incoming first years.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed states there is no registration or participation fee for the Peer Mentor Program and its activities and meals are at no cost to participants.
cards.access_notes: For incoming first-year students who apply and are accepted; consult the program page for its annual application dates.

cards.title: Walk Reed Canyon trails
cards.subtitle: Reed College’s 28-acre campus watershed
cards.notes: Take an unhurried walk on established trails and pause at the bridges; keep wildlife distant and leave the habitat as you found it.
cards.short_summary: A campus watershed walk with trail and wildlife guidelines.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed’s visitor guidance invites visitors to Reed Canyon and directs them to stay on established trails; it lists no admission or purchase requirement.
cards.access_notes: Privately owned by Reed; follow visitor guidance, including staying on established trails. Alcohol and fires are prohibited.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten distinct Reed study environments, from open library seating to reservable media-production rooms.

cards.title: Hauser Library Open Seating
cards.subtitle: Library main building
cards.notes: Bring your materials to any unreserved library table, desk, carrel, or comfortable seat; wireless access reaches most of the building.
cards.short_summary: Flexible open seating surrounded by Reed’s print collection and research support.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed states that study desks, carrels, and comfortable seating are distributed throughout the library, and that wireless access is available throughout most of the building.
cards.access_notes: All seating except assigned thesis desks is open to the Reed community; do not reserve or leave belongings at open desks.

cards.title: South Stacks Collaborative Work Area
cards.subtitle: Hauser Library, south end of South Stacks
cards.notes: Use the first-come collaborative area when your work needs a shared surface and whiteboards; bring a group or spread out a project.
cards.short_summary: A library collaboration zone with desks and whiteboards.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed Library identifies an open collaborative work area at the south end of South Stacks that is first come, first served; its map lists whiteboards and desks.
cards.source_title: Thesis Desks, Group Study Rooms, & Lockers — Reed Library
cards.access_notes: First come, first served; the library map identifies the collaborative space on LL1.

cards.title: Pollock Room
cards.subtitle: Hauser Library, main level
cards.notes: Set up near current newspapers and magazines when you want a reading-focused pause between research tasks; check the library map for location.
cards.short_summary: A main-level library room alongside current periodicals.
cards.evidence_claim: The Reed Library map lists the Pollock Room on the main level with current newspapers and magazines.
cards.source_title: Library Maps & Call Number Locations — Reed Library
cards.access_notes: Located on the library’s main level; consult current library access and hours before visiting.

cards.title: Hauser Library Group Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Hauser Library, level 2
cards.notes: Reserve a group study room in advance for a focused two-hour session; choose this option when your project needs a contained shared room.
cards.short_summary: Reservable library rooms for Reed community group work.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed Library offers four group study rooms for Reed students, faculty, and staff; reservations can be from 30 minutes to two hours, up to two hours per day.
cards.source_title: Thesis Desks, Group Study Rooms, & Lockers — Reed Library
cards.access_notes: Reservation only for Reed students, faculty, and staff; only one room may be booked at a time.

cards.title: Language Lab (L033)
cards.subtitle: Hauser Library LL1, inside the IMC
cards.notes: Practice a target language, use language-learning resources, or attend drop-in tutoring; confirm the current schedule before heading to L033.
cards.short_summary: A staffed language-learning room with resources and tutoring.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed identifies the Language Lab as a multi-purpose space in room L033 on LL1 of Hauser Library, supporting language learning with resources and tutoring.
cards.access_notes: Open during regular IMC hours, with some extended evening hours; it may be reserved for classes or language-related activities.

cards.title: Instructional Media Center (L32)
cards.subtitle: Hauser Library LL1
cards.notes: Use the IMC when your coursework benefits from media resources or a computer-oriented setting; ask the desk about equipment and current access.
cards.short_summary: A lower-level media and computer resource facility with study space.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed describes the IMC as a multimedia, audiovisual, and computer resource facility in L32; the library hours page identifies IMC study-space access.
cards.access_notes: Located on lower level one of the non-library part of the building; the IMC and Language Lab are listed as closed for summer break.

cards.entity_name: PARC Room 327: AV Recording & Editing Workroom
cards.title: PARC Room 327
cards.subtitle: Performing Arts Resource Center
cards.notes: Reserve this room for course-related audio or video editing and recording; plan a concise two-hour block and use it for production rather than Zoom.
cards.short_summary: A reservable production workroom for audio and video coursework.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed says PARC Room 327 supports audio/video recording and editing, gives priority to course and assignment use, and uses first-come reservations.
cards.source_title: Rooms — Performing Arts Resource Center, Reed Library
cards.access_notes: Reserve in two-hour blocks; academic purposes receive priority, and the room is not for Zoom meetings.

cards.title: PARC Room 330
cards.subtitle: Performing Arts Resource Center
cards.notes: Book Room 330 to rehearse a presentation or coordinate media-heavy group work; its monitor, hookups, and whiteboard support structured sessions.
cards.short_summary: A reservable 12-seat workroom for presentations and group media work.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed lists Room 330 as a presentation and conference workroom with an LCD monitor, iMac and laptop hookups, and a whiteboard; it seats 12.
cards.source_title: Rooms — Performing Arts Resource Center, Reed Library
cards.access_notes: Reservations are first come, first served in two-hour blocks; academic purposes receive priority.

cards.entity_name: PARC Room 329: Video Viewing & MIDI Workroom
cards.title: PARC Room 329
cards.subtitle: Performing Arts Resource Center
cards.notes: Choose this room for independent video viewing or MIDI composition work; its separate stations and headphones suit projects needing focused media playback.
cards.short_summary: A specialized room for video viewing and MIDI composition.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed describes PARC Room 329 as a video viewing and MIDI workroom with three independent iMac and MIDI-keyboard workstations, plus headphones.
cards.source_title: Rooms — Performing Arts Resource Center, Reed Library
cards.access_notes: Use is oriented to the room’s video-viewing and composition workstations; confirm current PARC access before visiting.

cards.title: PARC Computer Lab
cards.subtitle: Performing Arts Resource Center
cards.notes: Work on a digital assignment at one of the lab’s iMacs, then use the printer, copier/scanner, or large-format flatbed scanner as needed.
cards.short_summary: A computer-based workspace with scanning and printing tools.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed lists the PARC Computer Lab as having fourteen iMacs, a Xerox printer and copier/scanner, a large-format flatbed scanner, and a library catalog workstation.
cards.source_title: Rooms — Performing Arts Resource Center, Reed Library
cards.access_notes: Check current Performing Arts Resource Center hours and access before planning computer or scanner use.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Named stops on the SE Woodstock Boulevard, SE 28th Avenue, and SE Steele Street corridors immediately beside Reed College.

cards.title: Crystal Springs Rhododendron Garden: walk the lake paths
cards.subtitle: SE 28th Avenue corridor, one block north of SE Woodstock Boulevard
cards.notes: Enter from SE 28th Avenue and follow the accessible paths around Crystal Springs Lake; check the city page for seasonal access details.
cards.short_summary: A nine-acre public garden beside the Reed and Eastmoreland edge.
cards.evidence_claim: Portland Parks & Recreation identifies this nine-acre garden at 5801 SE 28th Avenue, one block north of Woodstock and between Reed College and Eastmoreland Golf Course.
cards.access_notes: City-listed hours are Thursday–Tuesday 10 a.m.–5:30 p.m. and Wednesday 1–5:30 p.m.; admission is charged for most visitors.

cards.title: Green Drop Garage: handle a car errand
cards.subtitle: SE 28th Avenue corridor beside Reed College
cards.notes: Use this named SE 28th Avenue stop when a vehicle-service errand belongs in your trip; confirm services directly before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A nearby garage listed in Reed’s current conference handbook.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed College’s conference handbook lists Green Drop Garage at 5321 SE 28th Avenue.
cards.access_notes: Service availability and pricing are not stated in the handbook; contact the business before visiting.

cards.title: Taco Express Fresh: stop on Steele Street
cards.subtitle: SE Steele Street corridor, immediately north of Reed
cards.notes: Add this named food-cart stop to a route along SE Steele Street, then verify its current menu and operating details before ordering.
cards.short_summary: A Reed-listed food-cart destination on the campus’s north-side corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed College’s conference handbook lists Taco Express food cart at 2618 SE Steele Street.
cards.access_notes: Menu, prices, and hours are not stated in the handbook; verify before visiting.

cards.title: 808 Grinds: order at the food cart
cards.subtitle: SE 26th Avenue corridor, west of Reed College
cards.notes: Use the SE 26th Avenue location for a takeout meal; check the restaurant’s location page before leaving because hours vary by day.
cards.short_summary: A named 808 Grinds food-cart location on the west-side corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: 808 Grinds lists its Gigantic Brewing food-cart location at 5226 SE 26th Avenue and provides day-specific hours.
cards.access_notes: The business lists Monday–Tuesday 11 a.m.–8 p.m. and Wednesday–Saturday 11 a.m.–9 p.m.; the cart is at Gigantic Brewing.

cards.title: Laughing Planet: use the Woodstock location
cards.subtitle: SE Woodstock Boulevard corridor, east of Reed College
cards.notes: Plan a meal stop at the Woodstock branch and use the official location page to confirm the day’s hours or place an order.
cards.short_summary: A named café location directly on the Woodstock commercial corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Laughing Planet lists its Woodstock café at 4110 SE Woodstock Boulevard, Portland.
cards.access_notes: The official location page lists dine-in service and hours of 10:30 a.m.–8 p.m. Sunday–Monday and 10:30 a.m.–9 p.m. Tuesday–Saturday.

cards.title: Otto's Sausage Kitchen: visit the counter
cards.subtitle: SE Woodstock Boulevard corridor, east of Reed College
cards.notes: Make this a daytime food-market stop on Woodstock Boulevard; use Otto’s contact page to confirm the hours before your visit.
cards.short_summary: A named sausage kitchen and market on the nearby Woodstock strip.
cards.evidence_claim: Otto’s Sausage Kitchen lists its address as 4138 SE Woodstock Boulevard, Portland.
cards.access_notes: Officially listed hours are Monday–Saturday 10 a.m.–5 p.m. and Sunday 11 a.m.–5 p.m.

cards.title: Nudi: choose a noodle stop
cards.subtitle: SE Woodstock Boulevard corridor, east of Reed College
cards.notes: Use Nudi’s official page to review current dishes and plan a meal along Woodstock Boulevard before you set out from campus.
cards.short_summary: A named noodle restaurant located on the Woodstock corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Nudi lists its Portland location at 4310 SE Woodstock and describes a menu that includes noodles, pasta, and ramen.
cards.access_notes: The restaurant lists weekday service noon–3 p.m. and 4–9 p.m.; weekend service is noon–9 p.m.

cards.title: Papaccino's: make a coffee-house stop
cards.subtitle: SE Woodstock Boulevard corridor, east of Reed College
cards.notes: Include this named coffee-house address in a Woodstock Boulevard route, and verify the current menu and access details before going.
cards.short_summary: A coffee-house destination in the Woodstock business district.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed College’s conference handbook lists Papaccino’s coffee at 4411 SE Woodstock Boulevard.
cards.access_notes: The handbook confirms the address but does not state hours, menu, or prices.

cards.title: New Seasons: pick up groceries
cards.subtitle: SE Woodstock Boulevard corridor, east of Reed College
cards.notes: Use the Woodstock store for a grocery stop and check the official store finder for its current hours and listed in-store amenities.
cards.short_summary: A full grocery-market stop on the nearby Woodstock commercial corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: New Seasons Market lists its Woodstock store at 4500 SE Woodstock Boulevard and identifies an espresso bar and pizza among its amenities.
cards.source_title: New Seasons Market Store Hours & Locations
cards.access_notes: The store finder lists daily hours of 7 a.m.–11 p.m.; confirm details before travel.

cards.title: Safeway: combine groceries and pharmacy
cards.subtitle: SE Woodstock Boulevard corridor at SE 47th Avenue
cards.notes: Use this grocery stop for supplies or pharmacy needs; the official store page lists pickup, delivery, and pharmacy services at this address.
cards.short_summary: A Reed-adjacent Safeway on the Woodstock Boulevard corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Safeway identifies its store at 4515 SE Woodstock Boulevard as close to Reed College and states that it has a pharmacy.
cards.access_notes: The official page lists store hours of 6 a.m.–midnight daily; pharmacy hours differ by day.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Reed College traditions and recurring community events, selected for safe, all-ages-friendly participation or observation.

cards.title: Renn Fayre
cards.subtitle: End-of-academic-year celebration at Reed College
cards.notes: Look for the student-created annual theme and scheduled arts, music, and community activities; follow current college event guidance while attending.
cards.short_summary: A themed spring celebration that marks the close of the academic year.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed identifies Renn Fayre as a themed celebration at the end of the academic year, beginning with Thesis Parade and including music, softball, art, and fireworks.
cards.access_notes: College event; availability and attendance requirements vary by year.

cards.title: Thesis Parade
cards.subtitle: Library steps to the registrar’s office, Reed College
cards.notes: Watch for the formal procession celebrating submitted senior theses, or respectfully cheer participating seniors from the designated public route.
cards.short_summary: Seniors ceremonially deliver their completed thesis work.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed documents that Thesis Parade has seniors march from the library steps to the registrar’s office to celebrate turning in their theses.
cards.access_notes: Participation is for graduating students; viewing access depends on the year’s event plan.

cards.title: Paideia
cards.subtitle: Winter learning week at Reed College
cards.notes: Browse the annual course listing for a practical, creative, or academic session; classes are led by members of the Reed community.
cards.short_summary: A January tradition of community-led learning outside the regular curriculum.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed describes Paideia as its annual festival of learning, with 2026 classes taught by students, alumni, staff, and faculty.
cards.source_title: Paideia 2026: A Tradition in Three Classes
cards.access_notes: Reed community program; individual offerings and access vary each year.

cards.title: Reed Arts Week (RAW)
cards.subtitle: Annual campus-wide arts festival
cards.notes: Check the festival calendar for exhibitions, talks, readings, and performances, then choose an event with posted access details and venue information.
cards.short_summary: A student-curated festival connecting visual art, performance, and writing.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed’s event calendar describes RAW as an annual student-curated arts festival founded in 1990, presenting student and visiting artists’ work.
cards.access_notes: The cited RAW event states festival events are free and open to the public; verify the current schedule.

cards.title: Canyon Day
cards.subtitle: Reed canyon and Centennial Orchard
cards.notes: Join the organized restoration work party to remove invasive plants and plant natives; dress for weather and use the provided training and tools.
cards.short_summary: Reed’s longstanding community day of ecological restoration.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed calls Canyon Day one of its oldest traditions and says participants restore the canyon by planting native vegetation and removing invasive plants.
cards.access_notes: The 2026 listing states it is free, open to all ages, requires no experience, and provides tools, training, and food.

cards.title: Great Reedie Bake Off
cards.subtitle: Commons and Student Union, Reed College
cards.notes: Form or support a team when the next rounds are announced, and follow the event’s food-handling and audience instructions for the live challenge.
cards.short_summary: Teams tackle themed baking challenges before the Reed community.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed reports that community teams compete in the Great Reedie Bake Off through themed rounds, with a live final baking challenge.
cards.source_title: “Baking Bad” Team Triumphs in the 2026 Great Reedie Bakeoff
cards.access_notes: Event timing, team registration, and audience access vary by year.

cards.title: Renn Fayre Softball
cards.subtitle: Department teams during Renn Fayre
cards.notes: Find a department team’s game schedule and come ready to support its player-created name, roster, and friendly tournament spirit.
cards.short_summary: Departments field softball teams with deliberately inventive names.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed describes Renn Fayre softball as a long-standing tradition in which students and faculty members in each department create team names.
cards.source_title: Portland, Oregon: Reed College mini viewbook
cards.access_notes: Team participation and game access are organized around the annual Renn Fayre schedule.

cards.title: Boar’s Head Procession
cards.subtitle: Annual Reed alumni holiday party
cards.notes: Attend the alumni holiday gathering if eligible and observe the musical procession; check the current alumni events page for registration details.
cards.short_summary: A Reed holiday procession featuring song and a ceremonial boar’s head.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed Alumni Relations describes the Boar’s Head Procession as an annual spectacle at the college’s holiday party, with roots at Reed in the 1920s.
cards.access_notes: Alumni event; consult current Alumni Relations listings for attendance information.

cards.title: International Festival
cards.subtitle: International Student Club community celebration
cards.notes: Volunteer or attend when announced to experience student-led cultural sharing, performances, and community exchange across Reed’s international community.
cards.short_summary: An annual student-organized celebration of Reed’s international community.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed states that the International Student Club’s annual International Festival began in 2010 and brings students, faculty, and staff together for cultural exchange.
cards.access_notes: Community-wide event; current date, location, and volunteer arrangements are announced by International Student Services.

cards.title: Nitrogen Day
cards.subtitle: Reed College Quad and campus gathering spaces
cards.notes: Look for the annual science-community program and choose its supervised demonstrations, talks, or food activities according to posted event guidance.
cards.short_summary: A recurring Reed celebration devoted to the seventh chemical element.
cards.evidence_claim: A 2026 Reed alumni publication identifies April 22, 2026 as the seventh annual Nitrogen Day, organized by Reed’s American Chemical Society and American Nuclear Society.
cards.access_notes: Follow current organizers’ safety instructions for any science demonstrations.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Reed College, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A conservative, under-21-safe weekend sequence that starts with named Reed landmarks and extends to nearby public gardens and riverfront paths.

cards.title: Start at Blue Bridge
cards.subtitle: Eastern bridge across Reed Canyon
cards.notes: Use this named eastern canyon crossing to orient yourself between campus sides, then continue only on established paths.
cards.short_summary: A recognizable campus crossing over the canyon.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed’s style guide identifies blue bridge as the eastern bridge across the canyon; Reed’s homepage depicts students walking across it.
cards.access_notes: Follow campus and canyon guidance while moving through the area.

cards.title: Walk Reed Canyon’s established trails
cards.subtitle: 28-acre watershed at the heart of campus
cards.notes: Take a slow daylight walk on established trails, observe wildlife from a distance, and leave the watershed as you found it.
cards.short_summary: A campus watershed with Reed Lake, native plants, and pedestrian crossings.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed describes the canyon as a 28-acre campus watershed with established trails and asks visitors to stay on them, leave no trace, and observe wildlife from a distance.
cards.access_notes: Privately owned by Reed; visitors enter at their own risk. Stay on trails; alcohol and fires are prohibited.

cards.title: Get your bearings at Hauser Library
cards.subtitle: Reed’s library and archives
cards.notes: Locate a study seat, ask at the reference desk for the building map, and save the semester-hour schedule for later.
cards.short_summary: A central academic building with extensive collections and study space.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed’s guidebook lists semester hours and describes the library’s print collection, study space, public workstations, printers, and reference help.
cards.access_notes: Published semester hours vary during breaks and summer; confirm access before going.

cards.entity_name: Douglas F. Cooley Memorial Art Gallery
cards.title: See what is on view at Cooley
cards.subtitle: In Hauser Library
cards.notes: Check the current exhibition page before heading over, then allow time to view the work without rushing to the next stop.
cards.short_summary: Reed’s campus gallery presents rotating exhibitions and its art collection.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed states that the Douglas F. Cooley Memorial Art Gallery hosts four major exhibitions annually and houses the college’s permanent art collection.
cards.access_notes: A Reed exhibition page lists public hours as Thursday–Sunday, noon–5 p.m.; verify the current exhibition and hours before visiting.

cards.title: Plan a meal at Commons Café
cards.subtitle: Gray Campus Center
cards.notes: Review the current menu and weekend service window, then use the dining option that suits your schedule and dietary needs.
cards.short_summary: Reed’s flagship dining location, with changing food stations and weekend brunch and dinner service.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed identifies Commons Café in Gray Campus Center and publishes weekend brunch hours of 10 a.m.–2:30 p.m. plus dinner from 5–7 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Hours are subject to change during academic breaks; Reed directs visitors to check the dining site for updates.

cards.title: Stop by the Reed College Bookstore
cards.subtitle: Lower level of Gray Campus Center
cards.notes: Browse course and campus materials during an open weekday, and check posted announcements before making a special trip.
cards.short_summary: A nonprofit campus bookstore serving Reed’s academic needs.
cards.evidence_claim: The bookstore identifies itself as a nonprofit in the lower level of Gray Campus Center and posts weekday hours.
cards.access_notes: Posted hours are Monday–Thursday 9 a.m.–5 p.m. and Friday 9 a.m.–4 p.m.; it is closed Saturday and Sunday.

cards.title: Find the Watzek Sports Center
cards.subtitle: Reed campus recreation facility
cards.notes: Locate the facility on the campus map and check with Athletics, Fitness & Outdoor Programs before planning a workout or swim.
cards.short_summary: A campus facility with pool, courts, gyms, studios, and fitness spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed lists an indoor pool, squash and racquetball courts, saunas, weight room, gyms, dance studio, and martial arts room at its sports center.
cards.access_notes: Confirm current building hours and eligibility with Athletics, Fitness & Outdoor Programs before entering.

cards.title: Watch for a Reed Outing Club trip
cards.subtitle: Student-led weekend outdoor activity
cards.notes: Join the club email list, read the weekly trip details, and submit the sign-up form if a listed outing fits your experience.
cards.short_summary: Free student-led outings and skill sessions in the greater Portland area.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed says the student-led club plans weekly outings, provides transportation, and offers trips free to all Reed students.
cards.access_notes: Trip details are emailed weekly; trips normally occur Saturday or Sunday and use a sign-up lottery.

cards.title: Visit Crystal Springs Rhododendron Garden
cards.subtitle: 5801 SE 28th Avenue
cards.notes: Use the garden’s paths for a quiet daylight visit, checking its current admission policy and any weekend event restrictions first.
cards.short_summary: A nine-acre public garden surrounding spring-fed Crystal Springs Lake.
cards.evidence_claim: Portland Parks describes this as a nine-acre public garden with rhododendrons, azaleas, other plants, and a spring-fed lake that attracts birds and waterfowl.
cards.access_notes: Published hours are Thursday–Tuesday 10 a.m.–5:30 p.m. and Wednesday 1–5:30 p.m.; some weekend areas may be limited by special events.

cards.title: End with a Sellwood Riverfront Park walk
cards.subtitle: SE Spokane Street and Oaks Parkway
cards.notes: Take the paved or unpaved paths for riverfront views, and keep the visit land-based unless you have planned appropriate water recreation.
cards.short_summary: A public riverfront park with paths, a boat dock, picnic tables, and accessible restrooms.
cards.evidence_claim: Portland Parks lists riverfront views, paved and unpaved paths, a boat dock, picnic tables, and accessible restrooms at Sellwood Riverfront Park.
cards.access_notes: Published park hours are 5 a.m.–midnight.
